A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NeuralSurv work and provide readable methods, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–N. Retained content can be matched reliably across renumbering and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic survival experiments, benchmark evaluations, and a sample-size ablation in Section 5 and Appendix M.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds calibration evaluations, runtime measurements, and prior-sensitivity results.

M1.justification: The sigmoidal hazard model, Gaussian weight and Gamma baseline priors, Pólya–Gamma/Poisson augmentation, MAP linearization, and EM/CAVI procedures remain unchanged. Alternative priors and network configurations appear as experimental variants, without revising the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic survival generator and eight benchmark datasets: COLON, METABRIC, GBSG, NWTCO, WHAS, SUPPORT, VLC, and SAC3. The added runtime and prior-sensitivity analyses reuse existing datasets.

E2.justification: Sumo-Net and DQS join the ten retained deep comparators throughout the synthetic, central benchmark, and sample-size ablation comparisons (v2 Tables A3, A5, and A7). The CoxPH, Weibull AFT, RSF, and SSVM comparisons already existed in v1.

E3.justification: v2 adds D-Calibration and KM-Calibration to the existing C-index and IPCW IBS evaluation. New protocols measure COLON runtime at N = 25, 125, and 250 across three network configurations, and compare Gamma(1,1), Gamma(2,2), and Gamma(0.5,0.5) priors. Existing benchmark splits and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix M.3 adds prior-variance sensitivity experiments on COLON, METABRIC, and GBSG. Appendix K adds runtime comparisons across sample sizes and network configurations. These investigate prior dependence and computational scaling; the N = 250 ablation itself was already present in v1.

E5.justification: v2 introduces systematic chi-squared D-Calibration testing, reported p-values, and rejection decisions at 0.05 across experiments. Table A11 also reports posterior medians and 95% intervals for phi. The existing five-fold evaluation and 90% survival-function bands remain; no increase in repeated runs is documented.

E6.justification: All matched original C-index and IPCW IBS entries are retained. Substantial new results cover Sumo-Net, DQS, both calibration metrics, runtime, and prior sensitivity. For example, Table A11 reports COLON C-index values of 0.671 under the default prior and 0.593 and 0.512 under alternative priors; these are different settings, not a deterioration between versions.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.1, formal assumptions, EM/CAVI derivations, computational-complexity argument, and Appendix N proofs remain unchanged after matching equation numbering. Appendix J.3 supplies standard calibration-metric formulas and explanations without revising the theoretical framework.

C1.justification: The central Bayesian survival-model, scalability, calibration, and discrimination claims remain. The conclusion adds an explicit novelty claim for integrating established Pólya–Gamma/Poisson augmentation with Bayesian-network linearization, refining how the methodological contribution is positioned.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 newly interprets overlapping but shifted posteriors as mild-to-moderate prior sensitivity and emphasizes balancing flexibility with regularization. It also acknowledges fifth-place KM-Calibration performance alongside D-Calibration success. Existing limitations concerning factorization, local linearization, and full-dataset computation are retained.

D1.justification: Appendices J–K add implementation sources for Sumo-Net and DQS, SurvivalEVAL metric APIs, and configuration-specific runtime information replacing rough timing summaries. Core architecture, optimization, normalization, hardware, and NeuralSurv's MIT-licensed code availability were already documented in v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds references on sigmoidal point processes, calibration, SurvivalEVAL, Sumo-Net, and DQS. Sections 3 and 6 more explicitly attribute the augmentation and linearization components to prior work. The method-property summary also changes DeepSurv's Bayesian-uncertainty designation, while the broader literature-review structure remains.

P1.justification: Section 2 expands the survival-analysis introduction, adds a hazard-function subsection, and reorganizes normalization explanations. Attribution and conclusion passages are revised, Appendix M gains descriptive subsections, and acknowledgments are added. Most methodological and appendix prose is retained.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn with Sumo-Net replacing DeepSurv. Existing deep-comparison tables gain comparator rows, while new calibration panels, a runtime grid, and a prior-sensitivity table substantially expand the visual presentation. Retained tables are redistributed and renumbered.

improvement.justification: Direct calibration evaluations address v1's reliance largely on IBS to support its central calibration claim. Added competitors, prior-sensitivity experiments, and comparative runtimes substantially improve assessment of robustness and practical costs, including less favorable KM-Calibration findings. Localized reporting errors remain: Table A10 marks p = 0.759 as failing and p = 0.038 as passing despite its 0.05 threshold. These errors limit confidence in those annotations but do not outweigh the stronger empirical scrutiny and transparency.
